stem: A 3-year-old child presents after orofacial trauma; which tooth is most likely to be affected?
explanation: Anterior maxillary central incisor is the correct answer. In young children with orofacial trauma, the most commonly affected tooth is the anterior maxillary central incisor.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because mandibular canines are not the tooth most commonly affected in young children with orofacial trauma.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because the anterior maxillary central incisor is the tooth most commonly affected in young children with orofacial trauma.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because maxillary second molars are not the usual teeth injured in this age group and injury pattern.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because mandibular first molars are not the typical teeth affected in orofacial trauma in a 3-year-old child.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because mandibular lateral incisors are less commonly affected than the anterior maxillary central incisor in young children with facial trauma.
